Subject: Hosted API — projected monthly ingestion + spike plan (recap & next steps)

Hi Lena / Alex —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what I heard and the asks we agreed on: 

- Baseline monthly token estimate: 150–200M tokens/month (this is for the core conversational assistant + follow-up completions).
- Average tokens per request: ~550 tokens (combined prompt + response).
- Typical daily variance: weekdays heavier (60% of traffic), weekend tail.
- Planned peak window: 2–3 hour marketing-driven spikes ~10x baseline qps in early launches; outside of that expected steady-state RPS results in ~5–10k tokens/sec.
- Immediate budget target: $8k–$12k/month for hosted inference initially; target unit economics for procurement evaluation: $2.75–$3.50 per 1M tokens (net of any committed discounts).

Action items we committed to: 
1) We will produce a pricing sketch that shows: baseline/month, two slab options (committed vs burst), and a modeled $/1M token for each slab. Attach: redwood-pricing-cheatsheet.pdf (outline).
2) You will share the more detailed volume CSV so we can run a tighter SLO/cost simulation (Alex — that spreadsheet you mentioned).
3) Karthik will map expected 99th/95th token latencies for the two slab options and note where Dedicated would be recommended if spikes exceed the hosted burst profile.

I’ve attached a quick cheatsheet and a blank volume template (granite-volume-profile.xlsx). If the numbers above look off, reply with corrected baseline/peak assumptions. Otherwise we’ll aim to send a tailored hosted pricing sketch by tomorrow EOD PST.

Thanks —
Priyom

Thanks Priyom — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline monthly tokens: more likely toward the lower end, 120–140M for Q3 (we’re conservative until launch).
- Spikes: our launch promo could create a short-duration 6x–8x request spike for ~90–120 minutes; that maps to an expected short peak of ~200 RPS with ~650 tokens per request (we over-provision for complex outputs).
- Budget: the leadership team has allocated $6k–$9k for the immediate POC phase; if unit econ hits <= $3.00/1M tokens we can push to $10k+/mo.

I attached the initial export of our daily request counts (see attached spreadsheet). If you can model a plan that keeps tail-costs predictable and a clear path to Dedicated for sustained higher spikes, we’re interested.

Alex
Product Ops, Granite Labs

Looping in quick technical cost/latency note to support the pricing sketch: 

- If average request = 650 tokens and peak short-window = 200 RPS, that’s ~130k tokens/sec during the spike. Hosted continuous-batching can absorb a lot of per-token inefficiency, but sustained spikes at that level push us toward a Dedicated recommendation for predictable 99th percentile latency under 250ms.
- For the initial hosted slab, two options I’d propose for the sketch: 
  a) Committed 150M/month @ $3.25/1M tokens (includes standard caching + 10% burst buffer), with ability to buy burst overage at $3.90/1M tokens up to 2x baseline.
  b) On-demand flex: no commit, baseline pricing $3.90/1M tokens, 1.5x burst cap at a hard throttle after that; preferred for teams with tight up-front budgets.

I’ll surface sample latency percentiles and a short note on what triggers Dedicated (sustained >3x baseline peak for >6 hours/day for 3 consecutive days).

—Karthik
Engineering, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the spreadsheet — that helps a lot. Next steps from our side: 

1) Pricing sketch: we’ll send two clean options (Committed slab + On-demand flex) with modeled monthly cost at 120M / 150M / 200M token tiers and a separate spike-cost appendix showing the delta if the short-window peak (200 RPS @ ~650 tokens) runs for 1h / 2h / 4h. Expect in your inbox by 2028-05-18 18:00 PST.
2) Telemetry checklist: we’ll include the minimum instrumentation we’d like (per-route token counters, 95/99 latency hooks, and early fallback policy) so Granite can validate SLOs during the POC.
3) Calendar: booking link if you want a follow-up once you review: https://cal.com/priyom/30min?ref=GRT-3412

If leadership is leaning to the lower budget band, call that out explicitly and we’ll bias the sketch toward On-demand flex + conservative burst caps. Otherwise we’ll show math that hits sub-$3/1M at the 150–200M committed tier.

Thanks —
